headline: Brief dry spell tonight, then wet, windy systems through Tuesday and into the weekend.
summary: A brief ridge of high pressure brings a dry spell tonight before a line of Pacific systems crosses western Washington through Tuesday. A long plume of moisture, an atmospheric river, is aimed our way, and a low near British Columbia may keep the wet pattern going into the weekend. Tonight should be mostly dry, with fog in spots and lows in the upper 30s to mid 40s. Tuesday is the wettest and windiest stretch, with gusts of 35 to 45 mph on the coast and north of Whidbey Island, plus snow in the high mountains. Highs stay in the 50s and low 60s, and river flooding isn't expected, though soils will become saturated. Forecasters are less sure about the Friday-into-weekend system, whose timing and strength could still change.
changes: Compared with the afternoon discussion, forecasters now describe a moisture plume aimed at the area and mention possible minor coastal flooding Wednesday morning from high tides in the San Juans and Whatcom County. The weekend system is now flagged for close watching, with its timing and strength still open.
